title: Game building is easy. Balance is hard!
author: MachinesWithThoughts
selftext:
I've built a few games this year and getting a basic engine up is trivial with AI and getting it looking nice is easy too. However, one part which I have the hardest time with is proper game balance. 

Adding new features such as loots, shops, tech trees, maps are quick but making them work together is the part that makes a good game really compelling. I've even created a few studies on random numbers, optimizing difficulty curves, hand-coded levels with feature gates and so on. But it all seems to be actual hard work, requiring proper thought and planning - isn't AI supposed to take that all away :-)!

I'm joking of course, but I think one thing anti-vibe coders miss is that the work never went away - it just shifted into another aspect of coding a good game that is often hidden. People focus on the surface stuff and not realize that it takes tons of time to make a good game work well.

comments.author: Agile_Branch_8743
comments.body:
Gen AI can't game design, it can just borrow elements from other games.

Can you share some of the games that you've built for reference?

replies.author: MachinesWithThoughts
replies.body:
I built a drug wars clone for grins and it was way too easy, even after I pointed out the issues.

I'm also building another remake of dungeon raid. The basic classic game is pretty good but adding additional features needs to be carefully scheduled into the game so the player doesn't level up too early. And I want to add other features to make the game more challenging on longer too but those have to also be balanced. I'm just playing and tweaking right now.

comments.author: david-song
comments.body:
It's very very difficult.

The big problem is that as you play your own game, you get better at it and are no longer qualified to playtest it from a beginner's perspective. Playtesters are worth their weight in gold, and the same thing applies to them - so spend them wisely.

comments.body: Yea im getting towards that part. Its easy to copybpaste the slop but making it your own and unique is in the details.

comments.body: Yeah I'm build a gnorp apologue style incremental game, getting the balance right is HARD, if it's too fast it's not satisfying, if it's too slow, it's not satisfying. If there's very little build variety it's not satisfying. It's quite difficult
